summary: Firecrawl is a comprehensive web scraping platform offering REST API + SDKs for scraping, crawling, search, and AI-powered extraction. The architecture centers on a multi-engine fallback system (fire-engine Chrome CDP/TLS, Playwright, fetch, document parsers) with feature-flag-driven engine selection. A Rust native module (firecrawl-rs) handles CPU-intensive HTML→markdown conversion, link extraction, sitemap parsing, and robots.txt compliance via NAPI bindings. The API layer (Node.js/Express) manages job queues (BullMQ/Redis/FoundationDB), concurrency limits, threat protection, billing, and webhook callbacks. Self-hosting is supported via Docker Compose but lacks the proprietary fire-engine anti-bot layer. With 159k stars, 10k+ commits, and daily active development, it's a mature, production-grade system.

- Media parsing: PDF, DOCX, ODT, RTF, XLSX → markdown/JSON
- Screenshots (viewport/full-page), PDF generation
- Robots.txt compliance (configurable)
- Threat protection (domain reputation, malware/phishing blocking)
- Zero-data-retention mode for sensitive data
- Cost tracking & billing integration
- Webhook notifications for async jobs

apiSurface: The Firecrawl API is primarily a REST API with multiple SDKs (Python, JS/TS, Go, Rust, Java, PHP, Ruby, Elixir, .NET, Dart). Core endpoints: v2/scrape (single URL to markdown/HTML/JSON/screenshots), v2/crawl (recursive site scraping with sitemap/discovery), v2/search (web search with content), v2/agent (AI agent that searches/navigates), v2/map (URL discovery), v2/batch-scrape (async bulk), v2/extract (LLM extraction). The SDKs expose `FirecrawlClient` (v2) with methods: `scrape()`, `crawl()`, `search()`, `map()`, `batchScrape()`, `extract()`, plus `interact()`, `agent()`, `research()`. Webhook support for async jobs. The native Rust layer (firecrawl-rs) provides high-performance HTML parsing, link extraction, sitemap processing, and robots.txt handling via NAPI bindings.
integrationPoints: For Veridian pipeline: 1) Use `/v2/crawl` with `includePaths`/`excludePaths` regex to target laptop product pages, 2) Use `formats: ["markdown", "json"]` with schema for structured spec extraction, 3) Leverage `actions` for pagination/JS interaction on dynamic catalogs, 4) Use `/v2/map` for rapid URL discovery before crawling, 5) Self-host to avoid fire-engine lock-in (use Playwright microservice), 6) Queue integration: submit crawl jobs via API, poll webhook/status endpoint, 7) Rust native lib (firecrawl-rs) can be used standalone for link filtering/sitemap parsing without full API, 8) Cost tracking helps budget scraping runs.
strengthsForVeridian:
- Mature, battle-tested at scale (159k stars, millions of pages/day)
- Multi-engine architecture handles JS-heavy laptop vendor sites
- Structured JSON extraction via LLM (schema-driven) matches Veridian's spec-extraction need
- Crawl + Map endpoints ideal for discovering + scraping product catalogs
- Actions support for pagination, infinite scroll, variant selection
- Self-hostable (avoids cloud lock-in, data stays local)
- Rust native parsers are fast and can be used independently
- Webhook-based async model fits ETL pipeline patterns
- Robots.txt compliance built-in
weaknessesForVeridian:
- Fire-engine (best anti-bot) is cloud-only; self-hosted relies on Playwright/basic fetch which may hit blocks on protected vendor sites
- Heavy infrastructure: requires Redis, PostgreSQL, Playwright service, optionally FoundationDB
- Proprietary fire-engine creates implicit lock-in for hardest targets
- Complex deployment (Docker Compose with 7+ services)
- Cost tracking/billing tied to their cloud model; self-hosted needs custom metering
- SDKs are API clients only — no local scraping engine
- LLM extraction adds latency and cost per page
